title: 唐詩八首
author: 李白、王維等
blurb: Eight famous Tang poems, most of them four lines long. A good first read.
note: Tang dynasty poems from the 8th century, in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Guo Xi, Early Spring (早春图), 1072. National Palace Museum, Taipei. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: 现代短文四篇
author: 许地山、胡适等
blurb: Four short modern pieces Chinese children read at school: peanuts at a family supper, Mr. Close Enough, a rickshaw puller, and three cats.
note: Published from 1919 to 1925, so it is in the US public domain (published before 1931). Lu Xun and Xu Dishan died over 70 years ago; Hu Shi (died 1962) and Zheng Zhenduo (died 1958) are public domain in China but may still be protected where copyright lasts 70 years after death. Xu Dishan's possessive 底 is printed 的, as in modern editions.
coverCredit: Attributed to Su Hanchen, Children Playing on a Winter Day (冬日婴戏图), 12th century. National Palace Museum, Taipei. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: 动物故事三篇
author: 鲁迅、爱罗先珂
blurb: Rabbits, ducklings and a lonely chick: two stories Lu Xun wrote in Beijing in 1922, and a fable by his blind Russian friend Eroshenko in Lu Xun's translation.
note: Published in 1922, so it is in the US public domain (published before 1931). Lu Xun died in 1936 and Vasily Eroshenko in 1952, more than 70 years ago.
coverCredit: Li Di, Chicks Waiting to Be Fed (鸡雏待饲图), 1197. Palace Museum, Beijing. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: 新诗六首
author: 徐志摩、胡适等
blurb: Six short modern poems from the 1920s, among them Xu Zhimo's Saying Goodbye to Cambridge Again and Dai Wangshu's Rain Alley. Short, musical and good for reading aloud.
note: Published from 1922 to 1928, so it is in the US public domain (published before 1931). Xu Zhimo, Liu Bannong and Dai Wangshu died over 70 years ago; Hu Shi (died 1962) is public domain in China but may still be protected where copyright lasts 70 years after death.
coverCredit: Ma Yuan, Walking on a Mountain Path in Spring (山径春行图), early 13th century. National Palace Museum, Taipei. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: 孔乙己
author: 鲁迅
blurb: Lu Xun's story of a failed scholar who drinks on credit at a village wine shop.
note: Published in 1919, so it is in the US public domain (published before 1931).
coverCredit: Lu Xun in Shanghai, 1 May 1933. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: 故乡
author: 鲁迅
blurb: A man goes back to his hometown after twenty years and finds it changed, and his childhood friend too.
note: Published in 1921, so it is in the US public domain (published before 1931).
coverCredit: Ma Yuan, Angler on a Wintry Lake (寒江独钓图), about 1195. Tokyo National Museum. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: 朝花夕拾 三篇
author: 鲁迅
blurb: Three of Lu Xun's memoirs of growing up: his nanny and the picture book she found him, the family garden and the old school, and his teacher in Japan.
note: Written in 1926 and published as a book in 1928, so it is in the US public domain (published before 1931). Lu Xun died in 1936, more than 70 years ago.
coverCredit: Attributed to Zhao Chang, Bamboo and Insects (竹虫图), Song dynasty. Tokyo National Museum. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: 朱自清散文四篇
author: 朱自清
blurb: Four of Zhu Ziqing's best-loved essays: on passing time, his father buying oranges at a station, a lotus pond by moonlight, and his five children.
note: Published from 1922 to 1928, so it is in the US public domain (published before 1931). Zhu Ziqing died in 1948, more than 70 years ago.
coverCredit: Unknown Song dynasty painter, Lotus Rising from the Water (出水芙蓉图). Palace Museum, Beijing. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: 春风沉醉的晚上
author: 郁达夫
blurb: A jobless writer in a Shanghai slum and the young cigarette-factory worker in the next room. Yu Dafu's story of two poor people in 1920s Shanghai.
note: Published in 1923, so it is in the US public domain (published before 1931). Yu Dafu died in 1945, more than 70 years ago.
coverCredit: Ma Lin, Waiting for Guests by Lamplight (秉烛夜游图), about 1250. National Palace Museum, Taipei. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: 狂人日记
author: 鲁迅
blurb: The diary of a man who thinks everyone around him wants to eat him. The first modern short story in vernacular Chinese.
note: Published in 1918, so it is in the US public domain (published before 1931).
coverCredit: Lu Xun at fifty, Shanghai, September 1930. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: 論語·學而
author: 孔子弟子
blurb: The first chapter of the Analects: sixteen short sayings about learning, in classical Chinese.
note: Composed more than 2,000 years ago, in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Confucius at leisure (孔子燕居像), anonymous. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: 西遊記 第一回
author: 吳承恩
blurb: The first chapter of Journey to the West. The Monkey King is born from a stone and sets out to learn how to live forever.
note: Written in the 16th century, in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Unknown Song dynasty painter, Gibbons Playing in a Loquat Tree (宋人枇杷猿戲圖). National Palace Museum, Taipei. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: 西遊記
author: 吳承恩
blurb: The Monkey King and the monk Tang Sanzang travel west for the scriptures. All 100 chapters of Journey to the West.
note: Wu Cheng'en, 16th century; public domain worldwide. Text: Wikisource, Shidetang-based edition.
coverCredit: A Qing court painter, Sun Wukong (孫悟空) in costume for the play Sizhou City, from the Office of Great Peace album of opera faces (昇平署臉譜), late Qing dynasty. National Library of China. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: 紅樓夢
author: 曹雪芹、高鶚
blurb: The rise and fall of the Jia family, and Baoyu and Daiyu. All 120 chapters of Dream of the Red Chamber.
note: Cao Xueqin (ch. 1-80) and Gao E (ch. 81-120), 18th century; public domain worldwide. Text: Wikisource collated edition (Gengchen base for 1-80, Cheng-jia for 81-120).
coverCredit: Sun Wen, the Garden of Grand View (大观园), 19th century. Lüshun Museum. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: 三國演義
author: 羅貫中
blurb: Liu Bei, Cao Cao and Zhuge Liang fight over what is left of the Han. All 120 chapters of Romance of the Three Kingdoms.
note: Luo Guanzhong, 14th century, in the Mao Zonggang revision; public domain worldwide. Text: Wikisource.
coverCredit: Shang Xi, Guan Yu Captures General Pang De (关羽擒将图), 15th century. Palace Museum, Beijing. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: 水滸傳
author: 施耐庵
blurb: 108 outlaws gather at Liangshan Marsh. All 120 chapters of Water Margin.
note: Shi Nai'an, 14th century; public domain worldwide. Text: Wikisource, the 120-chapter Yuan Wuya edition.
coverCredit: Zhang Lin, Hua Rong, from a painted album of the Water Margin heroes (彩绘水浒传), Qing dynasty. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.
